newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Goldman Sachs recommends selling kiwi dollar-NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs recommends selling kiwi dollar-NZPA.

text.p: United States investment bank Goldman Sachs is recommending that investors sell the kiwi dollar in favour of the Canadian dollar because of a divergence in monetary policies between the two countries, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Wednesday.

In a weekly commentary Goldman Sachs said that a tightening in monetary policy was likely in Canada after economic statistics there had continued to surprise on the upside, while a further easing in monetary policy was likely in New Zealand.
"We continue to recommend that investors exploit this monetary policy divergence by selling the New Zealand dollar against the Canadian dollar.
"As markets anticipate policy changes in these two countries the Canadian dollar should appreciate against the New Zealand dollar," Goldman Sachs said.
The report said that the New Zealand cross rate with the Canadian dollar should fall to 0.8050 Canadian dollars within the next three to six months from 0.8884 on Wednesday.
